Author: dwoitzik
Message:
fix(argocd): enable ServerSideApply for CRD-heavy Applications

system-manifests and homelab-apps ApplicationSet manage Traefik IngressRoute
CRDs. Client-side apply fails with 'resourceVersion: Invalid value: 0x0' on
patch operations because CRDs don't support strategic merge patches.
ServerSideApply lets the API server handle the merge.

Author: dwoitzik
Message:
fix(security): SEC-015 -- rotate leaked MikroTik terraform-user password (#295)

* fix(security): SEC-015 -- scrub leaked live MikroTik terraform-user password

network/scripts/bootstrap.rsc had the real, live password for the
'terraform' RouterOS API user hardcoded in plaintext -- committed to
this public repo since it was first added, and never rotated. This user
runs with read/write/api/rest/winbox policy (full network-management
access) and was never brought under Terraform's own management (no
routeros_user resource exists for it), so the leak had sat unnoticed
outside the usual gitleaks-baseline sweep (SEC-013).

Password rotated live on the router (by the account owner directly via
Winbox/SSH -- the terraform user's own policy correctly denies
'password'/'sensitive', so it can't rotate its own credential via API,
which blocked me from doing this remotely). Vault updated to match,
Atlantis LXC redeployed. Replaced the hardcoded value in this file with
a placeholder + a comment on how to set it safely going forward.

* chore(vault): rotate MikroTik terraform-user password (SEC-015)

Companion commit to the bootstrap.rsc scrub -- updates the encrypted
Vault value to match what was actually set live on the router, so a
future Ansible run doesn't revert Atlantis back to the old leaked
password.

* docs(audit): SEC-015 -- document MikroTik password leak and rotation

Author: dwoitzik
Message:
fix(security): remove live plaintext secrets missed by the original audit

This repo is public. A fresh gitleaks scan against the current working
tree (not just git history) found three live, currently-exploitable
plaintext secrets that the original 2026-06-19 history-based audit
missed entirely:

- Authelia OIDC client secret shared across FOUR clients (proxmox,
  pbs, argocd, grafana) - two of which (argocd-cm.yml,
  monitoring/application.yml) had the plaintext value committed
  directly. Worst finding so far: compromising it affects hypervisor
  and backup-server SSO, not just in-cluster apps.
- Grafana admin password, hardcoded in monitoring/application.yml.
- Garage S3 access key for Velero, in kubernetes/system/velero/secrets.yml
  - missed by the original scan because Garage's key format doesn't
  match generic AWS-key detector patterns.

All three converted to ExternalSecret-sourced references (matching the
existing Vault/External Secrets Operator pattern used elsewhere).
Cloudflare Tunnel token was also rotated today directly in the
Cloudflare dashboard (external, didn't need the cluster) and its
ExternalSecret added the same way.

Old values preserved in Ansible Vault (encrypted) so nothing breaks
once the cluster is back, pending the actual credential rotation -
that part still needs live Vault/Authelia/Garage access. Full status
and remaining work in docs/secrets-inventory.md.
